title: Cybersecurity Dataset Observatory
tagline: Discover Datasets for AI in Cybersecurity. Now all in one place.
description: An open catalogue of the network-traffic datasets used to train and evaluate AI for cybersecurity, from intrusion and botnet detection to industrial, vehicular and wireless security. For each dataset: what it contains, where to get it and the paper that introduced it.
lead: A curated catalogue of network-traffic datasets for AI-based cybersecurity: what each dataset contains, where it is distributed and which paper introduced it.
feature_title: A curated catalogue of network-attack datasets for AI
feature_text: Traffic datasets for intrusion detection, malware and C2 analysis and anomaly detection, linked to their original papers and distribution sources. Researchers can also submit new datasets.

citation.title: The AI Cybersecurity Dataset Observatory: Which data for AI in Cybersecurity?
citation.affiliation: University of Napoli Federico II, Italy

about: Many datasets are used to evaluate AI methods for intrusion detection, malware and command-and-control analysis, and anomaly detection, but the same dataset name often refers to different releases, captures and derived feature tables.
The Observatory records every dataset at the level of the **release and its distributed artifacts**, and links it to its original publication and distribution source.
eligibility: A dataset is included when it distributes recorded network communications (packet captures, flow records, wireless frames, CAN or V2X messages, protocol logs) or features demonstrably derived from them, whatever the security task. Host-only telemetry, malware binaries and sensor time series without a network-traffic component are not eligible on their own.

units.name: Family
units.text: A named line of related collections (e.g. the Stratosphere Malware Capture Facility).

units.name: Release
units.text: A documented distribution at a given stage (e.g. IoT-23 v1).

units.name: Capture
units.text: A single acquisition event or scenario inside a release.

units.name: Artifact
units.text: A file or package actually delivered to researchers (full PCAP, flow-only archive, CSV).
